significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that distinct SAE features encode harmful intent rather than merely sensitive topic, that manipulating those features changes refusal, and that monitoring them reduces benign over-refusal while retaining harmful-request detection. This establishes both a phenomenon—the claimed “substantially lower over-refusal than topic-based filtering”—and a mechanism—the “distinct monosemantic features for harmful intent versus harmful topic”—and the decomposition constrains explanations of both misuse detection and the exaggerated-safety behavior measured by XSTest (Röttger et al., 2024). Verified-false is distinguishable, but “intent and topic prove inseparable in feature space” would principally rule out clean separation by the chosen SAE representation, not internal separability in general, while “substantially lower” leaves the quantitative conclusion partly underdetermined. Topic substitution would not retain this score: generic mechanistic LLM safety is only the baseline, whereas the intent/topic decomposition is specifically sharper than the median refusal-feature hypothesis, though it remains bounded to a particular safety behavior rather than stating a transferable law.

reach.justification: The named handle is a “feature-monitor guardrail” built from a “small set” of intent features, providing an ex-ante filter that can flag or gate a harmful request before the model answers rather than merely explaining an observed failure afterward. Its downstream users could include deployers and safety auditors concerned with both harmful-request detection and XSTest-style over-refusal, and resources such as Gemma Scope (Lieberum et al., 2024) make this kind of SAE-based monitoring accessible beyond the originating analysis. After recalibration on another model, however, the conclusion supplies mainly a procedure for finding new features rather than a relation predicting what features or performance will be recovered; the claim itself warns that results may be “layer- and model-specific.” Topic substitution fails to preserve the score—the reach comes from the specifically deployable, low-false-positive intent monitor, not from LLM safety generally—so its ex-ante practitioner handle merits the lower edge of the 7–8 band despite limited cross-model transfer.
